method: Subtitle reflow rewrites only the cue text lines: the sequence number or identifier, the timestamp line, any cue settings and the order of the blocks are copied through as they are, and the file's line endings are normalised to LF. A cue's text is split into words; a line whose first non-space character is a hyphen, en dash or em dash starts a new run, so two-speaker dialogue keeps its break, and clearing the option merges every line of the cue. Each run is wrapped in two steps: greedy packing counts the fewest lines that hold its words inside the character limit, then the break points are chosen among those lines to minimise the sum of squared slack, the square of the limit minus each line width, so the words are spread as evenly as the line count allows. A word wider than the limit keeps its own line and is reported. Widths count visible characters: angle-bracket markup and an entity such as &amp; are kept in the output but use no character, so a styled line is measured as it renders, and the reading speed is the cue's visible characters divided by its duration in seconds. A cue is flagged when the reflowed text needs more lines than the maximum, when one word is longer than the line length, or when its reading speed exceeds the budget; flagged cues are still emitted, because shortening the wording is an editorial decision. Accepted limits are 5 MB of text and 5,000 cues, 10 to 100 characters per line, 1 to 5 lines and 5 to 60 characters per second, and blank, non-numeric, fractional or out-of-range settings are refused with the failing field named. Blocks without a valid timestamp line, and WebVTT NOTE, STYLE and REGION blocks, are passed through unchanged. The result is layout arithmetic on text the user supplies: it does not judge translation quality, caption sync or a platform's style guide, and it runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: W3C, WebVTT: The Web Video Text Tracks Format - cue timings, cue settings, cue identifiers and NOTE, STYLE and REGION blocks.
SubRip (.srt) caption format - sequence number, a timestamp line with a comma before the milliseconds and one or more text lines per cue.
BBC Subtitle Guidelines - line length and line count limits, balanced two-line breaks and reading-speed limits.
Netflix Timed Text Style Guide - characters per line, line count and characters per second limits used for subtitle delivery.
